tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved, and this is the most consequential marker placement in the set after packet 02. The marker is a preservative, not fragrance - PARFUM only appears at rank 15, well after it, which is exactly why section 3.1 defines tail_index as the EARLIEST tail-class member rather than as the fragrance position. The section 3.1 anomaly conditions do not fire (rank 11, and several conditioning ingredients precede it). The decisive consequence: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE at rank 12 is the formula's ONLY cationic surfactant, and it sits one rank below the marker, so this mask has zero cationic credit above the tail. Its whole above-tail conditioning architecture is silicone and lipid.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment (ranks 1-10) of the exact-market INCI; formula-only structural position.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Two of the three section 9.1 structural signals are satisfied - a rank-3 fatty alcohol and a five-species lipid breadth - which meets the written high threshold, even though the cationic axis contributes nothing. E2 ceiling: architecture, not delivered conditioning.
evidenceSignals: S1 not satisfied: zero cationic species above the tail; BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE is at rank 12, one below the marker at 11
S2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 3 of the full list (AQUA 1, GLYCERIN 2 precede it), inside the rank 2-3 window
S3 satisfied five-fold: ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE (6), BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (7), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (8), SIMMONDSIA CHINENSIS SEED OIL (9), PRUNUS AMYGDALUS DULCIS OIL (10)
Silicones DIMETHICONE (4) and DIMETHICONOL (5) are R2, not R4 lipids, and were not counted toward S3
Not counted (family 10): HYDROXYETHYLCELLULOSE (14), PEG-100 STEARATE (16), GLYCERYL STEARATE (17), the trideceth/laureth/polysorbate block, DISODIUM EDTA (24)
conditioningLevel.derivation: Section 9.1 S1/S2/S3 counting on the above-tail slice; 2 of 3 -> high.
thresholdReasoning: Why high, not moderate: the threshold is >= 2 of {S1,S2,S3} with no material counter-signal. S2 and S3 are both unambiguous, and S3 by a wide margin.
Why high, not low: low requires none of the three; two are satisfied.

Why confidence moderate rather than high: the section 9.1 confidence rule wants converging signals with no counter-signal, and there is a genuine structural counter-signal here - the category's primary conditioning axis (cationic deposition) is entirely tail-side. The two signals that fire are both from the lipid/fatty-alcohol side, so they converge less independently than the arithmetic suggests.
counterSignals: Zero cationic surfactant above the tail in a category whose conditioning axis is cationic-driven - a materially different architecture from the shelf norm
HYDROXYETHYLCELLULOSE (14) and the emulsifier block are rheology/infrastructure with zero credit; a thick rich feel here is partly rheology (lexicon family 10)
TEA-DODECYLBENZENESULFONATE (22) is an anionic surfactant, unusual in a rinse-out mask; tail-side, no credit assigned in any direction
limitations: Section 9.1's honest limitation applies, and this product exposes it: the S1/S2/S3 triple treats a silicone-plus-lipid architecture with no above-tail cationic as equivalent to a conventional multi-cationic rich mask. Whether that is the right reading is a calibration question.

weightPotential.rationale: The section 9.2 high anchor's required base fails because it is cationic-count-driven and this formula has no cationic above the tail; the low anchor fails because a cetearyl-class fatty alcohol sits in the top three. The residual is moderate. E2 ceiling. I flag this as the sharpest rule-versus-evidence tension I found - see limitations.
evidenceSignals: Required base leg 1 FAILS: zero distinct cationics above the tail (BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE at 12, marker at 11)
Required base leg 2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 3, inside the top three
Supporting alternative (a) would have been satisfied: BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (7) is an R4b butter above the tail, and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (8) is a named R4b heavy triglyceride

Supporting alternative (b) would also have been satisfied: DIMETHICONE (4) + DIMETHICONOL (5) is exactly the dimethicone/dimethiconol pair the anchor names as an occlusive silicone stack, both above the tail
Low-anchor leg 2 fails: CETEARYL ALCOHOL is a cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three
weightPotential.derivation: Section 9.2: high requires the base (both markers) plus at least one alternative. Base leg 1 fails -> high unreachable. Low anchor fails on its fatty-alcohol leg -> moderate residual.
thresholdReasoning: Why moderate, not high: the ruled structure makes the two cationic/fatty-alcohol markers a REQUIRED base and the lipid/silicone markers mere alternatives. This formula satisfies BOTH alternatives and only half the base, and the anchor gives no credit for that. One rank on the marker (Phenoxyethanol at 11 vs Behentrimonium Chloride at 12) is the entire difference.

Why moderate, not low: the low anchor is a three-way conjunction and its second leg is falsified by CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 3. The first leg (a single cationic species) is arguably satisfied by zero and the third (no R4b above the tail) is plainly falsified by shea butter at rank 7 - so low fails twice over.
The conflict fallback was not applicable: it resolves a formula-only HIGH against a lightness claim, and there is no high to resolve.
counterSignals: The evidence base says fatty-alcohol and butter load is the weight driver, not silicone or cationics - and this formula's butter/heavy-oil load above the tail is among the strongest in the set, yet the anchor cannot register it
Rheology (HYDROXYETHYLCELLULOSE) can make a formula feel heavy without being heavy - a reason not to reach past the anchor on feel
limitations: This is the clearest case in my set where the written anchor and the evidence rationale point in different directions. The section 9.2 anchors were ruled with the note that they are 'still first in line for checking against the calibration set'; this product is a strong argument for that check. I did not deviate from the written rule.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Above-tail architecture plus the section 9.5.2 hierarchy; product-name positioning used only as corroboration.

Step 6 smoothing clears both conjuncts: (i) dry surface control is the clearest practical differentiator - the silicone pair is the single most distinctive above-tail feature; (ii) the architecture extends materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct non-volatile silicone route (DIMETHICONE 4 + DIMETHICONOL 5), not a volatile carrier
primaryFocus.derivation: Section 9.5.2 in order; steps 3-5 all fail, step 6 clears. focus_care_verdict = nonspecific, which section 9.5.1's hard rule permits to resolve to smoothing precisely when the dry-surface route genuinely clears step 6.
thresholdReasoning: Why smoothing, not shine: shine and smoothing share M3/M1, and D2 forbids shine as a free add-on of the smoothing film. Independently, criterion 1's low-lipid-load conjunct is falsified - this is a rich nourishing architecture with a silicone route on top, which is precisely the formula shape section 9.5.4 says is NOT a gloss product.

Why smoothing, not general: general is step 8 and applies when nothing clears. Step 6 clears on both conjuncts, so the fallback is not reached. Note the standard's own wording: nonspecific resolves to general 'or to smoothing when the dry-surface route genuinely clears step 6' - this is that case.
Why smoothing, not moisture: D5's cluster guard fails at criterion 1 with a single glycerin, which is the exact anti-hero-token discrimination R9 was built for.

claim_role = corroborating: the product's own 'Smooth Anti-Frizz' name aligns with the selected focus. It was not needed - the route was selected on above-tail architecture alone - and under step 9 positioning may corroborate but never create.

The rich lipid stack means the same M1 observation also underlies softness and slip; only one focus slot is spent on it (section 6 rule 1)

assumptionNotes: Tail marker taken as PHENOXYETHANOL (11), the earliest tail-class member, not PARFUM (15). Section 3.1 is explicit that tail_index is the earliest member of any tail class, and the lexicon's marker-failure fallback (Parfum printed last by house convention) does not apply because Parfum is not last or penultimate here. This single decision removes the formula's only cationic surfactant from every structural signal.

DIMETHICONE and DIMETHICONOL counted as R2 silicones, never as R4 lipids for S3, and never as a weight driver in their own right (section 9.2: silicone presence is not the weight driver). They were counted only where the anchor names them explicitly - as alternative (b) - which never became reachable because the base failed.

TEA-DODECYLBENZENESULFONATE, LAURETH-23, TRIDECETH-3/-10, POLYSORBATE 60, PEG-100 STEARATE, GLYCERYL STEARATE all treated as family-10 infrastructure with zero credit; GLYCERYL STEARATE specifically flagged by the lexicon as a lipid-looking emulsifier.
DIGLYCERIN (13) treated as an R9-class humectant but is tail-side and therefore not counted toward the D5 cluster.
Anti-frizz positioning inferred from the product name only (E0) and used solely as corroboration for a focus already selected on architecture.

Review triggers I would fire: none of the mask-specific triggers is engaged. I would however flag weight_potential to the first-set review as the standard's open question 1 in concrete form - both weight-high alternatives are satisfied above the tail while the required cationic base is not.
No claims summary supplied. It would have mattered for shine criterion 3 (which fails on architecture anyway) and for a cleaner corroboration record on smoothing.
